blocks.text: Fashion Buyer — Fashion Business / Retail Management

blocks.label: Career category
blocks.text: Business, Finance & Entrepreneurship
QUALIFICATION
B.FTech / B.Des Fashion
Fashion Business / Retail Management
CAREER LEVEL
Entry to senior career
Buying assistance to merchandise and buying leadership

A Fashion Buyer selects the clothing, accessories, footwear, and other fashion products a retailer or brand should offer customers. Buyers combine fashion awareness with commercial judgement to decide what to buy, from whom, in what quantity, at what price, and for which season or customer segment.
They study trends, customer preferences, sales data, inventory, supplier offers, and budgets to create a product assortment that meets customer demand while supporting business profitability.
Typical responsibilities

items.text: Research fashion trends, competitors, customer preferences, and seasonal demand.
Select products, styles, colours, sizes, and price ranges for a target market.
Coordinate with designers, merchandisers, suppliers, sourcing teams, and retail planners.
Review product samples, quality, specifications, and commercial terms.
Negotiate pricing, order quantities, and delivery schedules where applicable.
Prepare buying plans and manage budgets within assigned categories.
Monitor sales, stock levels, sell-through rates, markdowns, and product performance.
Recommend replenishment, assortment changes, or discontinuation of underperforming products.

blocks.text: This career suits students interested in fashion, consumer behaviour, trend forecasting, business analysis, negotiation, and retail strategy.
B.Des / B.FTech — Fashion Business or Retail Management
Build fashion, merchandising, retail, and commercial foundations
Buying / Merchandising Intern
Assist with product research, samples, sales data, and assortment planning
Buying Assistant / Junior Buyer
Support category selection, supplier coordination, and order tracking
Fashion Buyer / Category Buyer
Manage product assortment, buying budgets, and commercial performance
Senior Buyer / Buying Manager / Head of Buying
Lead categories, buying teams, seasonal strategies, and commercial results
Progression depends on the retailer, product category, buying responsibility, and demonstrated commercial performance. Some organisations combine buying with merchandising or category management.
Year 1 — Fashion and business foundations
Academic focus

items.text: Fashion history, trends, and consumer culture.
Textile and garment fundamentals.
Principles of design, colour, and product aesthetics.
Introduction to retail management and business communication.
Basic mathematics, statistics, and spreadsheet skills.

blocks.text: Practical skills

items.text: Identify fashion product categories and target customer segments.
Analyse how different retailers position their products and prices.
Understand garment materials, construction, quality, and fit.
Compare product features, price points, and brand positioning.
Create basic product research and trend reports.

blocks.label: Suggested mini-project
blocks.text: Study a fashion retailer and prepare a report covering its target customers, product categories, price positioning, and seasonal assortment.
Year 2 — Merchandising and buying fundamentals
Academic focus

items.text: Fashion merchandising and retail operations.
Product lifecycle and seasonal assortment planning.
Pricing, costing, margins, and retail mathematics.
Inventory management and stock control.
Consumer behaviour and market research.
Supplier coordination and sourcing fundamentals.

blocks.text: Practical skills

items.text: Calculate retail price, gross margin, discount, and basic sell-through.
Prepare a product assortment plan for a defined customer segment.
Compare suppliers or product options against quality, cost, and delivery criteria.
Track stock availability and sales performance in Excel.
Understand the relationship between buying quantities and inventory risk.

blocks.label: Suggested mini-project
blocks.text: Build a seasonal assortment plan for a hypothetical fashion store, including product categories, sizes, price bands, and planned quantities.
Year 3 — Commercial buying and retail analytics
Academic focus

items.text: Buying strategy and category management.
Trend forecasting and consumer insights.
Sales forecasting and open-to-buy planning.
Vendor negotiation and supplier relationship management.
Merchandise planning, markdowns, and replenishment.
E-commerce merchandising and omnichannel retail.

blocks.text: Practical skills

items.text: Use sales history and trend research to justify product selection.
Prepare a buying budget and basic sales forecast.
Analyse best-selling and slow-moving products.
Evaluate margin, stock turnover, and markdown performance.
Present a buying recommendation using commercial evidence.

blocks.label: Suggested mini-project
blocks.text: Analyse a simulated sales dataset and recommend which products to reorder, reduce, or discontinue, explaining the expected commercial impact.
Year 4 — Industry application and professional readiness
If the programme is four years long, use this stage for advanced electives, industry training, and a capstone project.
Focus areas

items.text: Advanced category buying and assortment strategy.
Seasonal budgets, open-to-buy planning, and financial controls.
Supplier negotiations and commercial decision-making.
Retail analytics and product performance dashboards.
Sustainability, product traceability, and responsible purchasing.

blocks.label: Capstone project
blocks.text: Develop a buying plan for a fashion collection or retail category. Include trend research, customer profile, assortment selection, price architecture, buying quantities, margin estimates, supplier considerations, and sales-performance measures.
Industry preparation

items.text: Complete an internship with a fashion retailer, buying office, brand, or merchandising team.
Build a portfolio of assortment plans, buying reports, and data analyses.
Practise explaining product selections and buying quantities.
Learn to balance creative judgement with budget, stock, and profitability constraints.

blocks.text: Fashion and product knowledge
Trend awareness, fabric knowledge, garment quality, fit, product specifications, seasonal collections, and customer preferences.
Commercial and analytical skills
Sales forecasting, buying budgets, gross margins, inventory turnover, sell-through analysis, and markdown evaluation.
Negotiation and supplier coordination
Quotation comparison, price negotiation, order quantities, supplier relationships, sample approvals, and delivery coordination.
Customer and market understanding
Customer segmentation, competitor analysis, trend interpretation, shopping behaviour, and assortment decisions.
Communication and decision-making
Presenting buying recommendations, working with merchandising teams, prioritising products, and managing commercial trade-offs.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Seasonal assortment plan
Select products for a target customer, define categories and price bands, and allocate quantities across styles and sizes.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Assortment planning workbook and buying presentation.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Fashion retail buying budget
Estimate purchase costs, retail prices, gross margins, planned sales, and markdown scenarios.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Excel buying budget with documented assumptions.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Product sales analysis
Analyse simulated product sales to identify best sellers, slow-moving stock, and potential replenishment needs.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Sales analysis report or Power BI dashboard.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: Trend and competitor research
Study a product category, compare competing retailers, identify customer needs, and recommend an assortment direction.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Trend report with product and pricing recommendations.
Use public information or simulated datasets where necessary. Clearly distinguish assumptions from actual retail performance data.

blocks.text: Retail and fashion businesses such as Myntra, AJIO, Tata CLiQ, and Shoppers Stop can be starting points for researching buying, merchandising, and category-related career paths. These are examples to investigate, not confirmation of current openings; responsibilities vary by company.
What to learn during an internship

items.text: How buyers research trends and select products.
How product samples and quality specifications are reviewed.
How budgets, price points, and quantities are decided.
How buyers coordinate with sourcing, merchandising, and suppliers.
How sales data informs replenishment and future collection decisions.

blocks.text: Prioritise courses that include practical buying plans, budgeting exercises, and sales-analysis projects. A relevant portfolio and industry experience can be more useful than collecting multiple introductory certificates.
Further study can help with commercial strategy and leadership, but it is not essential for every buyer role.

blocks.text: Progression depends on category responsibility, buying budgets, commercial results, negotiation experience, and the size of the organisation. Some employers use buyer and merchandiser differently, so review the responsibilities in each job description.

blocks.label: AI-assisted trend analysis
blocks.text: Using digital tools to organise trend signals and support product-demand research, with human judgement guiding final selections.

blocks.label: Data-driven assortment planning
blocks.text: Combining sales, stock, customer, and product data to make more informed buying decisions.

blocks.label: Omnichannel buying
blocks.text: Coordinating product selections across physical stores, websites, and marketplaces.

blocks.label: Personalised product selection
blocks.text: Using customer insights to tailor product ranges to different segments.

blocks.label: Sustainable fashion buying
blocks.text: Considering material choices, product durability, traceability, and responsible sourcing.

blocks.label: Faster fashion cycles
blocks.text: Responding to changing demand while managing lead times, inventory exposure, and markdown risk.

By graduation, a career-ready candidate should be able to demonstrate:

items.text: Strong understanding of fashion products, consumer preferences, and retail trends.
The ability to create a product assortment for a defined customer segment.
Basic competence in buying budgets, pricing, margins, and inventory analysis.
Practical Excel skills and familiarity with retail reporting tools.
The ability to explain product-selection and buying-quantity decisions using evidence.
A portfolio containing assortment plans, trend research, and commercial analyses.
Professional communication and collaboration skills.

blocks.label: Recommended first target
blocks.text: Aim for a Buying Assistant, Junior Buyer, Fashion Merchandising Assistant, or Merchandise Planning Intern role. Build experience in assortment planning, sales analysis, and buying budgets before progressing toward a Fashion Buyer position and eventually buying leadership.
